Vs.

full_judgment: 14. The construction of a title document is a question of law. Findings of fact arrived at by misconstruction of a document are liable to be set aside in second appeal but only when the said document was a document of title and was the foundation of a suit, being in the nature of a contract or a document of title and hence the construction of a kabuliyat or the construction of an entry in a khatian used as a document of title or the construction of a deed, purporting to be a deed of gift would amount to a question of law (Refer 120 I.C. at page 557). In the instant case the court of appeal below arrived at the finding of fact to the effect that the gift was not a void gift as it purported to take effect in future by reserving the usufruct was arrived at on a misreading and misconstruction of the document of gift and upon a wrong view of the law, causing an error of law affecting the merits of the case and thus it needs to be set aside. The finding of the court of appeal below as to possession was also arrived at only on a consideration of the fact that as the gift was void there could not be any question of possession on the strength of the gift which was again erroneous as it was arrived at without taking into consideration the presumption of correctness attached to an entry in the R.S. khatian and without taking into consideration the evidence as to the possession of the plaintiff evidenced by the entry in the R.S. khatian and the evidence on record and without taking into consideration the legal position that even a possession under a document of title which subsequently proved to be a void document, would create a title in favour of the possessor if possessed for a period of more than 12 years, by adverse possession. On the premises above I find enough substance in this appeal and the said need to be allowed.
